lines.text: Not many Americans know that their country nearly doubled in size overnight, for less than three cents an acre.
cap: for less than three cents an acre

lines.text: In 1803, Louisiana was not a state. It was a French territory stretching from the Gulf of Mexico to Canada: over two million square kilometres.
lines.say: In eighteen oh three, Louisiana was not a state. It was a French territory stretching from the Gulf of Mexico to Canada. Over two million square kilometres.
cap: stretching from the Gulf of Mexico

lines.text: President Jefferson wanted just one city: New Orleans, the port that controlled the Mississippi River. He was ready to pay up to 10 million dollars for it.
lines.say: President Jefferson wanted just one city. New Orleans, the port that controlled the Mississippi River. He was ready to pay up to ten million dollars for it.
cap: up to 10 million dollars for it

lines.text: But Napoleon had a problem. He was losing Haiti to a slave revolt, and a war with Britain was coming. He needed money, fast.
So he offered the Americans all of it. Every acre of Louisiana, for 15 million dollars.
lines.say: So he offered the Americans all of it. Every acre of Louisiana, for fifteen million dollars.

lines.text: That is about 380 million dollars today. Roughly 18 dollars per square mile.
lines.say: That is about three hundred and eighty million dollars today. Roughly eighteen dollars per square mile.

lines.text: The land now covers all or part of 15 states, from Louisiana to Montana.
lines.say: The land now covers all or part of fifteen states, from Louisiana to Montana.

lines.text: An acre of Iowa farmland now sells for over 11,000 dollars: about 400,000 times what Jefferson paid.
lines.say: An acre of Iowa farmland now sells for over eleven thousand dollars. About four hundred thousand times what Jefferson paid.

lines.text: Still the best real-estate deal in history.
